questions.prompt: St. Justin Martyr addressed his First Apology -- a reasoned defense of Christianity -- directly to which audience?
choices: The Roman Emperor and Senate
The Jewish Sanhedrin
The bishops of Asia Minor
The philosophers of Athens alone
questions.explanation: Justin addressed his First Apology to the Emperor Antoninus Pius and the Roman Senate, arguing that Christians were being punished unjustly for a faith that was reasonable and good.
questions.hint: He wrote directly to the very government that could execute him for it.

citations.quote: Always be ready to give an explanation to anyone who asks you for a reason for your hope, but do it with gentleness and reverence.

To the Emperor Titus Aelius Adrianus Antoninus Pius Augustus Caesar, and to his son Verissimus the Philosopher, and to Lucius the Philosopher... and to the sacred Senate, with the whole People of the Romans

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Perpetua and St. Felicity, martyred at Carthage around 203 AD, died alone, without any companions.
questions.explanation: Perpetua, a young noblewoman, and Felicity, her slave, were martyred together in the arena along with several companions -- their shared witness, not solitary death, is what the Church has always remembered.
questions.hint: One was a noblewoman, the other her slave -- they were not alone in the arena.

citations.quote: Martyrdom is the supreme witness given to the truth of the faith: it means bearing witness even unto death.

citations.reference: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity

questions.prompt: St. Irenaeus of Lyons argued that the true teaching of the Church could be verified by tracing the bishops of his own day back, generation by generation, to whom?
choices: The apostles
The Roman Senate
The local synagogue
Secret Gnostic teachers
questions.explanation: Irenaeus's argument in Against Heresies -- that unbroken succession from the apostles guarantees the truth of a bishop's teaching -- is the same doctrine of apostolic succession the Church still teaches.
questions.hint: He was tracing the line back to its source: the men Christ himself commissioned.

citations.quote: In order that the full and living Gospel might always be preserved in the Church the apostles left bishops as their successors. They gave them their own position of teaching authority.

citations.reference: St. Irenaeus of Lyons, Against Heresies
citations.quote: The blessed apostles, then, having founded and built up the Church, committed into the hands of Linus the office of the episcopate... In this order, and by this succession, the ecclesiastical tradition from the apostles... have come down to us.

questions.prompt: The early Christian writer Tertullian famously wrote that the blood of martyrs is the ____ of the Church.
questions.explanation: Tertullian's line -- that persecution, rather than destroying the Church, caused it to grow -- captures how the early Christians understood martyrdom as fruitful witness rather than defeat.
questions.hint: He meant that persecution, instead of destroying the Church, made it grow.

citations.quote: Martyrdom is the supreme witness given to the truth of the faith: it means bearing witness even unto death.
We multiply whenever we are mown down by you: the blood of Christians is seed.

questions.hint: Two wrote in their own defense; two died for refusing to renounce Christ.

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Justin Martyr taught that 'seeds of the Word' -- fragments of truth -- could be found even among pagan philosophers before Christ.
questions.explanation: Justin's idea of the 'logos spermatikos' held that the divine Word had scattered seeds of truth throughout human thought before the Incarnation -- an early expression of the truth that God's light reaches every person.
questions.hint: His idea is called the 'logos spermatikos' -- the Word had already scattered seeds of itself through human reason.

citations.quote: The true light, which enlightens everyone, was coming into the world.

questions.prompt: St. Justin Martyr's First Apology (c. 155) describes the Sunday gathering in detail. Why does that description matter?
choices: It shows the shape of the Mass — readings, homily, intercessions, offering of bread and wine, thanksgiving, distribution — already fixed by the mid-second century
It is the first description of a Christian funeral
It proves the liturgy was originally in Latin
It shows there was no fixed order of worship
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the shape of the Mass — readings, homily, intercessions, offering of bread and wine, thanksgiving, distribution — already fixed by the mid-second century
questions.explanation: Justin is explaining Christian worship to a hostile emperor, so he has no motive to invent continuity. A Catholic reading his account recognises the structure of Sunday Mass immediately, which is a stronger argument for liturgical continuity than any later assertion.
questions.hint: He is describing it to outsiders, which is why the detail is trustworthy.

questions.prompt: True or False: Tertullian's question 'What has Athens to do with Jerusalem?' expressed the settled view of the Fathers that philosophy has no place in theology.
questions.explanation: False. It expressed Tertullian's view, and it was not the settled one — Justin held that seeds of the Word were scattered among the philosophers, and the Cappadocians and Augustine used philosophy extensively. Tertullian is a Father, not the Fathers, and quoting him as though he spoke for all of them misrepresents a genuine disagreement.
questions.hint: Ask whether other Fathers agreed with him on this.

questions.prompt: Origen produced the ____, a six-column parallel edition of the Old Testament comparing the Hebrew with Greek versions — an early monument of textual scholarship.
questions.explanation: The name means 'sixfold'. Origen's willingness to compare the Hebrew against the Greek, and to note where they differed, is the ancestor of critical biblical scholarship — undertaken by a man usually remembered for allegory.
questions.hint: The Greek prefix for 'six' gives the name.

questions.explanation: Two of these looked outward to argue with the wider world and two looked inward to secure the Church's own reading of Scripture. Both tasks were already necessary within a century of the apostles.
questions.hint: Two are apologists addressing outsiders; two are chiefly concerned with Scripture and succession.

questions.prompt: St. Athanasius of Alexandria spent much of his life defending the teaching of which council against the Arian heresy?
choices: The Council of Nicaea (325)
The Council of Chalcedon (451)
The Council of Trent
The First Vatican Council
questions.explanation: Athanasius was Nicaea's fiercest and most persistent defender, insisting for decades that the Son is 'consubstantial' with the Father against Arius's claim that Christ was a created being.
questions.hint: He spent decades defending one word: that the Son is truly, fully God.

citations.quote: God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God, begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father.

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Athanasius was exiled from his own see multiple times because of his unwavering defense of Christ's full divinity.
questions.explanation: Athanasius was driven from Alexandria five separate times as the political tide shifted for and against Arianism -- his persistence against overwhelming opposition gave rise to the phrase 'Athanasius against the world.'
questions.hint: His persistence against nearly everyone earned him a famous Latin phrase.

citations.quote: God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God, begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father.

questions.prompt: St. Basil the Great, St. Gregory of Nazianzus, and St. Gregory of Nyssa are together known by what title, reflecting their shared defense of Trinitarian doctrine in the 4th century?
choices: The Cappadocian Fathers
The Latin Doctors
The Apostolic Fathers
The Desert Fathers
questions.explanation: Named for their home region in Asia Minor, the Cappadocian Fathers refined the Church's language for the Trinity and defended the divinity of the Holy Spirit affirmed at the Council of Constantinople.
questions.hint: Two brothers and a close friend, all from one region in modern-day Turkey.

citations.quote: And in the Spirit, the holy, the lordly and life-giving one, proceeding forth from the Father, co-worshipped and co-glorified with Father and Son, the one who spoke through the prophets.

questions.prompt: True or False: St. John Chrysostom taught that honoring Christ in the Eucharist is inseparable from caring for Christ in the poor.
questions.explanation: Chrysostom preached forcefully that it does no good to honor Christ's Eucharistic body while neglecting his body in the poor -- a teaching the Catechism still draws on when it links the Eucharist to charity.
questions.hint: This teaching is what the Catechism still draws on today when it links receiving the Eucharist to how we treat the poor.

citations.quote: To receive in truth the Body and Blood of Christ given up for us, we must recognize Christ in the poorest, his brethren.

citations.reference: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew
citations.quote: Do you want to honor Christ's body? Then do not scorn him in his nakedness, nor honor him here in the church with silken garments while neglecting him outside where he is cold and naked.

questions.prompt: St. Jerome's greatest labour was the Vulgate. What made his approach distinctive?
choices: He translated the Old Testament from the Hebrew rather than from the Greek Septuagint, against considerable opposition including Augustine's
He translated from Latin into Greek
He worked entirely from the Septuagint
He produced the first vernacular translation
questions.correctAnswer: He translated the Old Testament from the Hebrew rather than from the Greek Septuagint, against considerable opposition including Augustine's
questions.explanation: Augustine worried that going behind the Septuagint would unsettle congregations who knew it. Jerome went to the Hebrew anyway. The disagreement is a useful corrective to the idea that the Fathers formed a единый bloc — they argued, in writing, at length.
questions.hint: The controversy was about which language he translated from.

citations.reference: St. Jerome, Prologues to the Vulgate

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Basil the Great founded a complex outside Caesarea providing housing, a hospital and care for the poor — an early institutional charity.
questions.explanation: True; it became known as the Basiliad. The same bishop who wrote against the Arians on the divinity of the Spirit built a hospital, and the Fathers generally saw no distance between those two activities. Chrysostom makes the same point when he says honouring Christ in the Eucharist is inseparable from honouring him in the poor.
questions.hint: He is remembered for a monastic rule, a doctrinal fight, and a building.

questions.prompt: St. Gregory of Nyssa taught that the soul's approach to God is an endless progress into greater love — a doctrine known by the Greek term ____.
questions.explanation: From Paul's straining forward to what lies ahead. Since God is infinite, arrival is not the shape of the journey: the blessed go on receiving more of him for ever, and satisfaction and desire increase together rather than one ending the other.
questions.hint: The word comes from Philippians 3:13, 'straining forward'.

citations.reference: St. Gregory of Nyssa, Life of Moses

questions.hint: One is defined by exile, one by breadth of activity, one by preaching, one by trinitarian precision.
